notes: 36 assigned files read in full, no partners. Many style hits in this chunk are already in the known ledger (policy.go literal/order/&&/one-line calls, registry.go &&/inline calls/literal/order/save prefix, sessions.go prefix/dup/&&, evals.go Dir comment/dup loop/regexp, shell.go RunSync copy, config.go LoadFragment copy, installenv.go order/literal, plist.go order, routines bools, sched_windows literals, launchctl anonymous table, installenv_test/policy_test t.Run bodies) and were not re-reported. Dropped on re-check: policy_test two-scenario CheckPolicy tests (RULE-GOLANG-TEST-007 prefers plain asserts for one or two cases); named error variables (statErr/readErr/showErr) and by-value Policy/Rule structs are pervasive pre-existing package patterns, so legacy under the guide's ENFORCEMENT scope. Cross-chunk note for the station: sched_windows.go Start now passes schedule.Intervals, which is nil for an Unscheduled routine, into TaskXML; whether TaskXML/the server Start path guards that lives outside this chunk (correctness, not style).

findings.claim: The new LoadFragment returns errors "reading %s: %w" (L218) and "parsing %s: %w" (L222) without the Component.Method: prefix RULE-GOLANG-ERR-001 requires; every other error in config.go outside the legacy Load/Save (Settings.get, Settings.set, McpServerNames, McpServer) carries its function prefix, so a malformed repo fragment surfaces as a bare 'parsing <path>: ...' with no hint that LoadFragment (marker expansion) produced it.
findings.evidence: Re-read internal/config/config.go L195-L243 at the pinned head: LoadFragment L212-L225 is new in this diff (git diff hunk @@ -207,6 +207,23); its two fmt.Errorf calls carry no 'LoadFragment:' prefix. Load (L195-L208) has the same unprefixed shape but is pre-existing, so only the new function is in scope. Not the known ledger row on this file (LoadFragment duplicating Load) — that one is about the parallel body, this one about the message contract; folding the two into one function would still have to choose a prefixed message.
findings.fix: Prefix both messages: fmt.Errorf("LoadFragment: Failed to read %s: %w", path, err) and fmt.Errorf("LoadFragment: Failed to parse %s: %w", path, err).

findings.claim: New early-return guard blocks are followed by code with no blank line: refreshIfChanged's `if isMissingAndUnloaded { return }` (L92-L94) runs straight into the next `if err == nil && ...` guard at L95, and Repo.Validate's Name guard (L43-L45) runs straight into the new reserved-name comment and check at L46-L48. RULE-GOLANG-ERR-002 requires a blank line after every early-return guard block when code follows; the rest of registry.go (Add L143-L148, Remove L192-L195, readRegistrySnapshot) follows it.
findings.evidence: Re-read internal/repos/registry.go L35-L58 and L85-L102 at the pinned head; both spots are added lines in this diff (refreshIfChanged is new; the reserved-name block L46-L50 is inserted directly after the pre-existing Name guard, whose blank line now sits after the new block instead, so the guard at L43-L45 has no blank line before L46). Not in the known ledger for this file (known rows cover the && condition at L95, inline shell.Run calls, the composite literal argument, 'archived' literal, type/const order and the save prefix).
findings.fix: Insert a blank line after L94 and after L45.

findings.claim: The SyncAll doc comment was extended without reflowing: L17 now reads just '// Called once at' and the sentence continues on L18 ('// server startup: ...'), leaving a stray short line in the middle of the godoc paragraph that every other doc comment in the package wraps at full width.
findings.evidence: Re-read internal/routines/bootstrap_darwin.go L13-L22 at the pinned head; the diff hunk @@ -11,7 +11,10 shows the old line '// and not disabled ... Called once at' was split, the new text inserted, and the 'Called once at' tail kept on its own line. Purely a formatting defect of a changed comment.
findings.fix: Reflow L17-L18 into one wrapped paragraph: '// (the config server's Start writes it) before it is ever bootstrapped.\n// Called once at server startup: a logout tears down the gui domain and ...'.

findings.claim: The package doc still says evals load 'from evals/<skill>-<date>/ (nightly routine) or evals/<skill>-<hex>/ (matrix mode) directories' (L4-L5), while this change makes LoadForSkill also read the nested evals/<skill>/<date>-<hash>/ layout and makes ManifestStub emit that nested path as the default output — the package-level description now omits the layout new manifests write to.
findings.evidence: Re-read internal/evals/evals.go L1-L6, L217-L272 and L277-L289 at the pinned head: LoadForSkill's own doc (L217-L222) and EvalDir's doc (L33-L34) were updated for the nested layout, ManifestStub's Output (L285) is now filepath.Join(evalsDir, skillName, "<date>-<hash>", "eval.json"), but the package comment L1-L5 was not touched. Distinct from the known ledger row on this file, which targets the EvalDir.Dir field comment at L37.
findings.fix: Extend the package doc: '... from flat evals/<skill>-<date>/ (nightly routine) or evals/<skill>-<hex>/ (matrix mode) directories and nested evals/<skill>/<date>-<hash>/ run directories, each holding eval.json plus an optional deltas.json.'

findings.claim: TestFingerprint declares its own `run := func(args ...string)` git closure (L288-L292) that duplicates the closure inside gitRepoWithAgentWorktrees (L262-L266) line for line except the -c user.email/user.name config; the next test needing to mutate the fixture repo will copy it a third time.
findings.evidence: Re-read internal/repos/registry_test.go L256-L307 at the pinned head: both closures build append([]string{"-C", repo, ...}, args...), run exec.Command("git", ...).CombinedOutput() and require.NoError(t, err, string(output)); TestFingerprint is new in this diff (hunk @@ -151,2 +274,37). The -c identity flags are harmless for the branch/worktree calls TestFingerprint issues.
findings.fix: Extract a package-level test helper `gitRun(t *testing.T, repo string, args ...string)` (with the -c identity flags) and call it from both gitRepoWithAgentWorktrees and TestFingerprint.
